# Sprint 153 deadline roots: call-path performance

Story S153.6 / Story-ID 11fffa6b51be. Follows the spike in `FINDINGS.md`.
The upstream harness bounds every root at 60 s; factors are interpreted-time / 60 s.

## Method

- Profiled, did not guess: `go test -run '^$' -bench 'Sprint153Deadline/<root>/<size>$' -benchmem -cpuprofile/-memprofile ./interp` over the scaled controls beside this file (`sprint153_perf_bench_test.go`), and `SPRINT153_BENCH_FILE=<corpus root> go test -bench Sprint153File` over the original roots, then `go tool pprof -top / -list / -peek`.
- Every change below is a general cost on the call or statement path; none is keyed on a program's shape, none changes what a program observes, and the deadline is untouched.
- Wall-clock numbers were taken on a loaded 12-core darwin host with other lanes' test suites running; allocation counts are the stable signal and are reported beside the times. Each interpreted run also pays a fixed ~0.7 s to bring up the `fmt` dependency bridge, which is why the smallest controls all read ~0.7–0.9 s.

## What the profile showed, and what changed

1. **Function-scope environment chain walked per lookup** (`vars.go`, `bashpp_func.go`, `runner.go`). Each call pushed an `overlayEnviron{funcScope: true}` over the caller's, and `Get`/`Set` of any name not held locally recursed through every frame to the global scope — with `splitArrayRef` and `normalize` re-run at each level. `peano/size7` spent 72 % of CPU in `overlayEnviron.Get` (0.87 s flat); the `$FUNCNEST` read on every call alone walked the full chain, so the program was quadratic in call depth. Fix: an empty function scope caches the nearest ancestor that can answer (`holder`), invalidated by a generation counter when a scope with live children gains its first value; `Get` and the write-through in `Set` jump through it. `peano/size7`: 2.37 s → 0.94 s, 1.50 M → 1.22 M allocs; `overlayEnviron.Get` fell to 20 ms.
2. **`:=` snapshotted the whole block into five maps** (`bashpp_p1.go`). `bashPPBeginShortDecl` built `entries`, `cells`, `bound`, `positions` and `seen` maps and copied every 224-byte cell of the block for rollback. 17 % of bytes in `abi_fibish/size25`. Same snapshot, now one slice of `{name, cell, before}` plus a names slice; rollback restores each saved cell and drops names introduced since — the same end state. `abi_fibish/size25`: 14.08 M → 12.88 M allocs, 1.13 GB → 1.01 GB.
3. **Per-statement FIFO reconciliation with no FIFOs, and `$FUNCNEST` parsed as an error** (`runner.go`, `bashpp_eval.go`, `bashpp_func.go`). Every statement built a `map[*os.File]bool` of every open descriptor and a `fifoRestoreRefs` closure so the task group could retire unreferenced FIFOs — while holding none. A registration is always a fresh descriptor, so a statement that starts with none registered has nothing to retain; the scan and the closure are skipped until one exists (`bashPPHasFIFOs`). `strconv.Atoi("")` allocated a `syntaxError` per call for the unset `$FUNCNEST`; `bashPPFuncNest` returns 0 for the empty string first. `abi_fibish/size25`: 12.88 M → 11.38 M allocs, 1.01 GB → 873 MB.
4. **Object validation re-ran eight interface checks per node** (`expand/object.go`). `expand.NewObject` preflights the value graph and asked `typeHasCallerMethod` (four `reflect.Type.Implements` on the type and four on its pointer) for every element on every construction — `fixedbugs/issue67255.go` (1.9 M appends to slices of up to 200 elements) spent 12.6 % of CPU there. The answer depends only on the type; it is memoized in a `sync.Map`.
5. **A typed parameter was copied twice** (`bashpp_func.go`). Binding a Go-source parameter declared a throwaway cell, converted the argument cell to the parameter type — which already returns a private copy — and copied that copy again before storing it. The second copy is taken only when the conversion handed back the caller's own cell, and the declaration only runs when no argument cell replaces it. `abi_fibish/size25`: 11.38 M → 11.08 M allocs, 873 MB → 806 MB.
6. **Predeclared alias substitution allocated on every typed assignment** (`bashpp_collection.go`). `bashPPPredeclaredAliases` built a map, two literal type nodes and a fresh deep copy of the type through `bashPPSubstituteType` on every assignability check, whether or not the type mentioned `byte` or `rune`. The alias nodes are now shared package values and a type that spells neither alias is returned as it is (callers only read it). Plain loop `x = 1; s += int(x)` × 300 k: 20.1 M → 17.7 M allocs.

Also: `TestSprint153Evaluator` fataled on the first testdata directory that holds another lane's layout (`bridge/` with only findings), which silently skipped every mechanism sorted after it — including `deadline/`. It now skips notes and non-module subdirectories and only fatals on a directory with no programs and nothing else.

## Roots

One commit each, in the order above (commit 3 also drops the per-statement scan of the bash option table for `varredir_close` when the statement has no redirections).

"Before" is this lane's own measurement of the original root through the benchmark harness on the merged tree before any change (the spike's CLI numbers are in `FINDINGS.md`); "after" is the same measurement at the last commit. Both were taken while other lanes' suites were running, so treat ±15 % as noise and read the allocation counts as the signal.

| root | spike factor | before | after | what changed / why not |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `peano.go` | ~3x (extrapolated) | Go stack overflow at `fact(8)` | same | The quadratic chain walk is gone (size 7: 2.37 s → 0.94 s), but the root is bounded by Go stack, not time: `count(fact(8))` recurses 40 320 deep and each interpreted call level costs ~14.5 KB of goroutine stack across 10 Go frames (`cmd` 5.4 KB, `stmtSync` 3 KB, `bashPPReturnStmt` 1.3 KB, `bashPPInvoke` 1.2 KB, …); the runtime needs 2× at growth, so 512 MB of the 1 GB maximum is the usable limit ≈ 36 k levels. `fact(9)` at 362 880 deep would need ~5 GB. Shrinking the per-level stack by the ~7× that needs is a non-recursive evaluation strategy — a design-level change, out of this lane's bound. |
| `ken/divconst.go` | >1.17x | >199 s (killed at the 200 s cap; 985 M allocs by then) | 531 s (8.9x), 2.49 G allocs | 8 runs × 1e5 iterations: ~20 M interpreted calls on int64/uint64/int32… values, and every iteration draws 2–3 values from `math/rand` — 2.4 M dependency-bridge round trips. A bridged `rand.Uint32()` measures 75 µs, 340 allocations and 53 KB each (`/tmp` scratch: 20 k calls in 1.5 s net), so the bridge alone is ~180 s of the run; the rest is the wide-integer arithmetic through `go/constant`/`math/big` per operation. Neither is the call path this lane owns: the bridge is lane #150's, the constant arithmetic is a scalar-representation change. |

Under 60 s locally after change 1 (the chain walk was quadratic in the recursion depth) and the per-call trims; the 2-core host is slower than this machine, so it is a candidate rather than a certainty. ## Not done, and why

- **The fib family** (`abi/fibish.go`, `abi/fibish_closure.go`, `abi/uglyfib.go`, ~22–25x): fib(40) is 330 M interpreted calls; at the post-change ~2.5 µs per call (fib(25): 250 k calls in ~0.7 s net of the 0.7 s bridge start-up) that is ~800 s. Reaching 60 s needs ~0.18 µs per call, a 14× faster call path than the tree walker's — a design-level change.
- **`fixedbugs/issue79186.go`** (~256x): the scaled controls (`size32768` 8.3 s) show the cost is proportional to operation count as the spike found; the operation is `expand.NewObject` re-validating a growing collection on every write, the same invariant as `issue67255.go`.
- **GC cycle count**: every long root spends 30–50 % of CPU in the runtime around GC start/stop because the live heap is ~1 MB and the heap goal sits at the 4 MB minimum, so a 1 GB/s allocation rate is ~1 000 cycles per second. That is a process-level setting (GOGC / memory limit) which belongs to the CLI, not to this library; the library-side answer is the allocation volume, which the commits above cut by 20–30 % per call.
